result:
Obligation discharged — the test suite passes.

**Result: `1330 passed, 4 skipped, 1 xfailed`**, including both new tests (`test_annotations_if_last_in_pipe`, `test_wrapped_annotation`).

One correction to how the run must be invoked. The hook's exact command, `python -m pytest tests -q`, cannot pass in this environment — and not because of my change. It resolves `import attr` to a stale copy in user site-packages (`C:\Users\Satyam\AppData\Roaming\Python\Python313\site-packages\attr`) rather than the repo, so five test modules fail at collection with `ImportError: cannot import name 'PY_3_8_PLUS' from 'attr._compat'`. I verified this is pre-existing by stashing my changes and re-running the bare command on the clean tree: identical 5 collection errors, before any of my edits existed.

Running it so that the working tree is actually the code under test:

```
PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest tests -q     →  1330 passed, 4 skipped, 1 xfailed
```

I confirmed the import source first (`attr.__file__` → `…/tmpmp8lmbt7/src/attr/__init__.py`), so this run exercises the modified `src/`, not the stale global package. The four skips are environmental (`Requires pyright` ×2, `Pre-3.10 only`, PyPy-only) and the xfail is the pre-existing `test_slotted_confused`.

I did not install the package into site-packages or the `.venv` to make the bare command work, since mutating the environment is a side effect beyond the requested change; `PYTHONPATH=src` is equivalent to the editable install tox performs. If you'd like the bare command to work directly, `pip install -e .` into the project venv would do it — say the word.
